question: How did a group of MIT students make money from a Massachusetts lottery called Cash WinFall?
answer: By spotting a flaw in its rules. When the jackpot passed two million dollars without a winner, the prize money rolled down to smaller prizes, and in those weeks a ticket was worth more than it cost. Buying hundreds of thousands of tickets in those weeks, the students made a steady, legal profit.
move: Work out the expected value before calling any bet a bad one.
simply: Lottery tickets normally lose money. But in special weeks this lottery paid out more than it took in, and the students bought huge numbers of tickets.
why: Expected value is the right way to judge any bet, insurance or deal: what you'd get on average, not just whether you might win.
source: Jordan Ellenberg, How Not to Be Wrong, 2014
reference: Jordan Ellenberg, How Not to Be Wrong: The Power of Mathematical Thinking (Penguin Press, 2014)
